summary: Defines a DHCPv6 option that lets a relay agent pass RADIUS authorization and identification information to a DHCPv6 server. The access server acts as both relay and RADIUS client, adds the RADIUS response to forwarded client messages, and the server uses it to reply appropriately.

eli5.summary: A doorman checks your ID and writes a note, then hands the note to the person who gives you a room.

questions: nas as dhcpv6 relay and radius client
what is the dhcpv6 radius option
how does a nas act as dhcpv6 relay and radius client
subtitle: Lets a relay agent that is also a RADIUS client hand RADIUS authorization data to a DHCPv6 server.

tldr.problem: When the DHCPv6 server is not co-located with the RADIUS server, the server has no way to see the authorization data the RADIUS server gave the access server.
tldr.mechanism: A new DHCPv6 option, OPTION_RADIUS (81), carries selected RADIUS attributes from the relay agent to the server inside Relay-Forward messages.
tldr.outcome: The server can use those attributes to pick configuration for the client. Only attributes in an IANA registry may be carried, and the option is invisible to clients.

today: RFC 7037 is a Proposed Standard, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it according to the metadata for this unit. It remains the definition of the DHCPv6 RADIUS option.

sections.title: Why the Server Needs RADIUS Data
sections.content:
DHCPv6 lets a server give clients stateful parameters such as IPv6 addresses and prefixes, and stateless ones such as DNS information or the name of an Address Family Transition Router. In this RFC's scenarios, the DHCPv6 server sits in the central part of an ISP network.

RADIUS is widely used for centralized authentication, authorization and user management in broadband access networks. It can authorize the Network Access Server (NAS) to assign an address or prefix from a pool, or with an explicit value. When the DHCPv6 server and RADIUS server share a place, they may share a user database. When they do not, the relay agent needs a new way to pass the authorization information to the server. This RFC provides it.
sections.eli5: The doorman knows what you are allowed, but the person giving out rooms works in a different building. They need a way to share the note.

sections.title: Network Scenarios
sections.content:
In both scenarios the NAS plays two roles at once, DHCPv6 relay agent and RADIUS client. The DHCPv6 server is not co-located with the RADIUS server, but both are in the same administrative domain.

For IP over Ethernet (IPoE), the client's Solicit triggers an Access-Request to the RADIUS server. For PPP over Ethernet (PPPoE), a PPP LCP Config-Request triggers it. If RADIUS authentication or authorization fails, the sequence stops and the NAS does not forward the client's message to the DHCPv6 server. If it passes, the NAS MUST store the information from the Access-Accept for the whole session, and then forwards later DHCPv6 messages in Relay-Forward messages carrying OPTION_RADIUS.

On a RENEW (5) from the client, the NAS SHOULD NOT start a new Access-Request exchange. On a REBIND (6), it MUST, unless RADIUS capability is disabled on the NAS.
sections.eli5: The doorman checks your ID first. If it fails, you go no further. If it passes, he remembers the answer and passes it along each time you ask for something.

sections.title: The OPTION_RADIUS Format
sections.content:
The option has the code OPTION_RADIUS (81), an option-len giving the length of the data in octets, and option-data, a list of one or more RADIUS attributes copied from the Access-Accept message. Attribute formats come from Section 5 of RFC 2865 and Sections 2.1 and 2.2 of RFC 6929. If several attributes share a type, their order MUST match the order received from the RADIUS server.

Only attributes listed in the "RADIUS Attributes Permitted in DHCPv6 RADIUS Option" registry may appear. The initial entries are Vendor-Specific (26), Delegated-IPv6-Prefix (123), DS-Lite-Tunnel-Name (144), Framed-IPv6-Address (168), DNS-Server-IPv6-Address (169), Delegated-IPv6-Prefix-Pool (171) and Stateful-IPv6-Address-Pool (172). The option should appear in Relay-Forward (12) messages relaying SOLICIT (1), REQUEST (3) and REBIND (6), and may appear in others.
sections.eli5: The note is a list of facts the RADIUS server gave the doorman, kept in the same order, and only certain kinds of facts are allowed on it.

sections.title: Relay, Server and Client Behavior
sections.content:
Relay. If configured to send the option, and the Access-Accept contained permitted attributes, the relay MUST include OPTION_RADIUS in the Relay-Forward message. It adds the permitted attributes one by one, keeping order for same-type attributes.

Server. A server that supports the option SHOULD extract and interpret the attributes and use them to select configuration parameters for the client. A server that does not support it MUST silently discard the option.

Client. The option travels only between relays and servers. Clients are not aware of it, MUST NOT send it and MUST ignore it if received.
sections.eli5: The doorman writes the note, the room-giver reads it if they know how, and guests never see it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Known weaknesses of DHCPv6 and RADIUS may apply to their options. The main new risk is a compromised relay agent: by forging attributes in the option, an attacker could influence what the server assigns to clients. The RFC notes that in real deployments the NAS belongs to the same administrative domain as the DHCPv6 server.

RADIUS messages are encrypted, but DHCPv6 messages are always unencrypted, and some vendor-specific attributes might hold sensitive information. Administrators are strongly advised to keep such data out of DHCPv6 messages. If confidential vendor-specific attributes are needed, they should use IPsec with encryption, and relays and servers implementing this RFC MUST support IPsec ESP with encryption in transport mode.
sections.eli5: If the doorman were tricked, he could write a false note. And since the notes are not in a sealed envelope, secrets should not go on them.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA assigned OPTION_RADIUS (81) in the "DHCP Option Codes" registry. It also created the registry "RADIUS Attributes Permitted in DHCPv6 RADIUS Option" within the DHCPv6 registry group, with an allocation policy of Expert Review. The designated experts are told to consider carefully the security implications of letting a relay include new RADIUS attributes.
sections.eli5: An official list keeps track of the option's number and of which kinds of facts may go on the note.

fields.name: option-len
fields.desc: Length of the option-data in octets.
